summary.title: Demystifying CXL Memory with Genuine CXL-Ready Systems and Devices
summary.one_liner: Real CXL memory expanders on a 4th-gen Intel Xeon behave differently from DDR-emulated CXL (remote NUMA) memory, and a bandwidth-aware page allocation policy (Caption) can improve memory-bound workloads by up to 24%.
takeaways: Emulating CXL memory with DDR on a remote NUMA node differs from real CXL memory in several important ways.
Real CXL memory devices from three manufacturers were benchmarked on a 4th-gen Intel Xeon system.
Memory-bandwidth-intensive applications can benefit from adding CXL memory as a bandwidth expander.
Caption, a CXL-aware dynamic page allocation policy, converges to a favorable share of pages on CXL memory and improves such applications by up to 24% over the default NUMA policy.
summary.summary: The paper evaluates a true CXL-ready system built on the latest 4th-generation Intel Xeon CPU with three CXL memory devices from different manufacturers. The authors run microbenchmarks comparing real CXL memory against DDR-emulated CXL memory on a remote NUMA node, and analyze how the CPU and CXL memory interact. They identify workloads that benefit from CXL memory and propose Caption, a CXL-memory-aware dynamic page allocation policy that uses CXL memory as a bandwidth expander. The abstract reports up to 24% improvement for memory-bandwidth-intensive applications over the default NUMA page allocation policy.
